title: Choose the page structure
question: All three use the Tomato Flood world. They differ in how the page is built around the newsletter sign-up. Lock one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: Fly along
options.thesis: The sign-up is a boarding pass to Queenstown, and the page below is the itinerary.
options.viewport: Tomato flood: a handwritten 'Ga je mee?', the live days-to-go at poster scale, and a cream boarding pass beside it with name and e-mail fields and 'Stap in' as the button.
options.risk: Travel imagery is a common trope; the pass has to stay one simple form, not a costume.

raised.raise: One dotted route runs from the pass down the whole page and links every section like stops on the trip.
Photos sit in flat tomato, marigold and plum blocks on one module, never as loose rounded cards.
Handwritten asides hang in the margin beside the letter text, like notes on a printed page.

options.label: The open letter
options.thesis: The site reads as Ruben's open letter, and signing up means addressing the envelope.
options.viewport: A tomato band with 'Lieve vrienden,' in hand type and the days-to-go. The cream letter rises over it, and beside its opening sits the envelope with the address fields and 'Verstuur'.
options.risk: A letter invites long reading; the envelope must stay in view so the action never waits for the end.

options.label: Postcards home
options.thesis: Each section is a postcard from the road to Queenstown: a drawing on the front, Ruben's handwriting on the back.
options.viewport: One big postcard: the tomato front with mountains and 'Groeten uit Queenstown' turns to its cream back, with a short message on the left and the address lines (the sign-up) under a stamp on the right.
options.risk: Flipping cards can hide text; on phones every back must be readable without flipping.

options.label: Block identity
options.thesis: Photos and loud colour bars snap together under one module.
options.viewport: Tilted photo under stacked saturated bars.
options.risk: Corporate feel; would replace the Tomato palette.
options.case: Supporters don't recognise a design-studio identity, and it would push out the Tomato colours.
options.kept: Photos framed by flat colour blocks on one module.

options.label: Margin edition
options.thesis: Two text columns around a rail, with notes in a wide margin.
options.viewport: A small dense text block in a wide margin.
options.risk: Scholarly and cold for a personal letter.
options.case: Too academic for church friends and family.
options.kept: Handwritten asides hung in the margin.

options.label: One red line
options.thesis: One continuous line carries a life story through every fold.
options.risk: Museum tone, about objects rather than people.
options.case: The dotted flight route already plays this part, in the app's own language.
options.kept: One continuous route linking every section.

options.label: Night board
options.thesis: A text-mode board where presence is precious.
options.viewport: Title art over numbered menu lines.
options.case: No supporter identifies with a terminal.
options.kept: Showing who else follows along feels precious.

options.label: Segment clock
options.thesis: Digits as lit segments with ghost cells.
options.risk: Cold and technical, with a dark palette.
options.kept: The countdown changes instantly, with no slide.

options.label: Drawcord cape
options.thesis: One pull turns a flat plane into volume.
options.viewport: A black semicircle with a gold cord.
options.risk: Luxury fashion, unrelated to the mission.
options.case: No link to the move or the people.
options.kept: One clear action changes the whole form.
